name: Fox-Fire: three fires on one victim
targetName: one three-fire Fox-Fire volley on one champion
objective: Investigate high one three-fire Fox-Fire volley on one champion output under a finite setup; compare controlled item swaps instead of claiming a global maximum.
mechanic: Each first fire deals 40/60/80/100/120 + 0.4 AP magic, with subsequent hits reduced to 40%. Three fires on the same victim nominally weight 1 + 0.4 + 0.4 = 1.8 full fires, giving rank-5 total 216 + 0.72 AP. Movement speed is utility, not another damage multiplier.
finiteState: Level 18, selected ability maximum learned rank unless explicitly overridden, minute 30. Enemy champion: 3000 maximum HP, 100 armor and 50 MR. Owner HP 100%, target HP 100%, observation 3s. No dragons, elixirs or allied stat buffs. Record actual AD/AP, HP and resist modifiers; Gathering Storm at minute 30 if selected. No free permanent stacks. Stop damage at death, cap healing at recipient missing HP, and report raw output separately. Seraph legally transformed. One W creates exactly three fires, all actually hitting the same isolated champion within a three-second observation. No minions or other champions steal targeting; no Charm, Q, R or attack damage in score.
test: Compare one versus three connected fires at fixed AP/MR. Swap AP against penetration; repeat near another enemy to measure split targeting. Count damage events and verify reduced subsequent hits rather than multiplying the first hit by three.
limits: No three full-strength same-target hits, extra fires from movement duration, or Charm/attack setup damage added to W. Actual targeting and proc rules remain manual checks.
tradeoff: A clean isolated volley can be difficult around minions, and maximum AP may lose utility or haste.
